source: the questions a tax-return site asks before it asks for figures (MR-097); each yes points at the room that already holds the fact

questions.ask: Married at the end of the year?
questions.why: Married filing jointly has wider brackets and a double standard deduction.

yes.label: Set the filing status to married filing jointly

questions.ask: Children or other dependents living at home?
questions.client: Do children or other dependents live with you?
questions.why: Each child opens the child tax credit; one dependent opens head of household and the earned income credit widens.

yes.label: Count the dependents in Household facts

questions.ask: Paid for child care so you could work?
questions.client: Did you pay for child care so you could work?
questions.why: A share of what was paid comes back as the child and dependent care credit.

yes.label: Add what was paid for child care

questions.ask: Paid tuition or school fees for college?
questions.client: Did you pay college tuition or fees?
questions.why: All of the first 2,000 and a quarter of the next 2,000 come back as a credit.

questions.ask: Paid interest on a student loan?
questions.client: Do you pay on a student loan?
questions.why: Up to 2,500 of the interest comes off income before the brackets, while income allows.

yes.label: Add the student loan to the Debt room; its interest is worked out from the rate

questions.ask: Put money into a 401(k), IRA or similar this year?
questions.client: Did you put money into a 401(k) or IRA?
questions.why: Pre-tax money skips the brackets now, and at lower incomes the saver's credit gives a share of it back.

yes.label: Add the contributions on the pay row or an Investments account

questions.ask: Put money into a health savings account (HSA)?
questions.client: Do you put money into an HSA?
questions.why: Through payroll an HSA dollar skips federal, state and FICA.

yes.label: Add the HSA on the pay row or as an Investments account

questions.client: Do you earn 1099 or side income?
questions.why: It carries both halves of Social Security and Medicare, and every business expense comes off it first.

yes.label: Add the 1099 income and its business expenses

questions.ask: Own the home, with a mortgage or property tax?
questions.why: Mortgage interest and property tax count toward itemizing when they beat the standard deduction.

yes.label: Add the mortgage to the Debt room and the property tax paid as a deduction

questions.ask: Gave to charity, money or goods?
questions.why: Gifts count toward itemizing when the total beats the standard deduction.

questions.ask: Large medical bills, more than about a twelfth of income?
questions.client: Did you have large medical bills?
questions.why: Medical bills above 7.5 percent of income count toward itemizing.

questions.ask: Bought an electric car, solar, a heat pump or new windows?
questions.client: Did you buy an electric car or home energy upgrades?
questions.why: A share of what was paid comes back as a credit, capped.

questions.ask: A health plan bought on the marketplace (healthcare.gov)?
questions.client: Do you buy your health plan on the marketplace?
questions.why: The premium tax credit is settled on the return from the 1095-A; the room cannot work it out, so it is a note to carry in.

yes.label: Bring the 1095-A to the return; the credit is reconciled there
